claim: Harvey, Mazzoleni and Melone (NBER w33554, March 2025, revised January 2026, full text read): a one-standard-deviation increase in the Threshold (Calendar) signal lowers next-day S&P 500 futures returns by about 16 (17) bp and raises 10-year Treasury futures returns by 4 (2) bp; the pressure reverts within two weeks; Section 4 front-running spread portfolio (long S&P 500 futures / short 10y note futures, weight = average of modified Threshold and Calendar signals) has Sharpe above 1 over 1997-2023.
quote: Rebalancing pressures revert almost entirely within two weeks
limitations: Futures returns, close-to-close, not open-to-close; author-reported Sharpe with the authors' own cost estimate; multiple-comparison bias on signal windows flagged by the discussant; effect concentrated before the 2016 start of the local sample is not excluded.
independent_replication: QuantReturns replication (2025) reproduces the sign and roughly the size; no independent live record found.

claim: NBER abstract page (revision date January 2026): institutional rebalancing has a market-wide impact; equity returns fall 17 bp over the next day when stocks are overweight; cost to investors about 16 billion USD a year.
quote: When stocks are overweight, funds sell stocks and buy bonds, leading to a decrease in equity returns of 17 basis points over the next day.
limitations: Abstract only; close-to-close, not the overnight/intraday split that determines what a next-open fill can capture.

claim: Paper Section 4 defines the modified Calendar signal as sign(-Calendar) in the last week (5 days) of a month, a reversal term sign(Calendar_{-4}) on the first business day of the new month, and zero on any other day; the Threshold part is rescaled to -Threshold/1.5% so both signals have equal risk contribution.
quote: On any other day, the modified version of the signal is set to zero.
limitations: Paper normalises by 1.5%, QuantReturns by 0.012, and the paper places the reversal on the first business day; the preregistered candidate uses the task's version and the difference is a disclosed deviation.

claim: Parker, Schoar and Sun (NBER w28028, JF 2023): target date funds rebalance contrarianly between stocks and bonds within a few months; the flows reach stocks held through mutual funds and reduce their next-quarter returns.
quote: The rise of TDFs has moved a significant share of retirement investors into macro-contrarian strategies that sell stocks after relatively good stock market performance.
limitations: Quarterly horizon, cross-sectional stock effect; not a daily index timing rule; no Sharpe.
independent_replication: Cited by Harvey et al. as supporting evidence.

claim: Kent Daniel discussion slides (Red Rock 2025): the signal windows (thresholds 0.1-2.5 percent, calendar 5 days before month end) were selected among many, so the reported t-statistics are biased upward.
quote: Note that there is potentially a bias here as a result of multiple comparison, and the t-statistic should be corrected to account for this.

claim: Daniel: liquidity-provision anomalies (index inclusion, short-term reversal, leveraged ETF rebalancing) historically faded as competition rose, and the paper's 16 billion annual cost is a worst-case estimate.
quote: However, as competition between liquidity providers increased the profits associated with liquidity provision fell.
limitations: Historical analogy, not a test on this signal.

claim: QuantReturns replication (GitHub mirror of the 2025-07-03 article): Threshold signal averaged over deltas, divided by 0.012 and inverted; Calendar signal zero except the last five sessions of a month, minus sign for the first four, inverse of the 5th-last value on the last day; weight 0.6 Threshold + 0.4 Calendar; futures Sharpe 1.24 (1997-2025), 1.42 (2007-2025-06); SPY/TLT ETF version CAGR 15.62 percent, Sharpe 1.17, no costs.
quote: On the final day of the month, after all the rebalancing price pressure has finished, we assign the inverse value to that of 5th last trading day of the previous month.
limitations: Author self-computed, not peer reviewed, no transaction costs, both legs traded, close-to-close.
independent_replication: Reproduces the paper's shape; no third-party check.
